sections.overview: Danio rerio is a small freshwater fish native to South Asia.
sections.identification: Its name refers to the conspicuous dark horizontal stripes running along the body and onto the tail.
sections.habitat: It is recorded from slow or still waters, including streams, ponds, canals and rice-field habitats.
sections.diet: Wild fish eat small invertebrates, including worms, crustaceans and insect larvae.
sections.behavior: Field observations describe it among South Asian danionin fishes occupying freshwater sites with varied flow conditions.
sections.reproduction: FishBase reports year-round breeding in the populations covered by its species account.
sections.ecology: Studies of danionin fishes report insects as an important natural food resource, with diet varying among species and sites.
sections.conservation: FishBase displays a Least Concern assessment dated 2009; this is an older assessment, not a current population survey.
